notices.title: GBE PPE Procurement

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Great British Energy is seeking to appoint a supplier for the provision of Personal Protective Equipment, workwear and corporate clothing for employees undertaking site visits and other operational activities. The requirement will establish an ongoing supply arrangement covering a range of safety equipment and clothing, including protective footwear, high-visibility clothing, safety helmets, gloves, safety glasses, thermal clothing and corporate workwear. The arrangement will support existing employees, new starters and the replacement of items due to wear and tear, damage, sizing requirements or changing operational needs.
As part of this requirement, the selected supplier must be able to provide delivery to Great British Energy's headquarters in Aberdeen within one hour when required. We therefore particularly welcome interest from suppliers based in Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire, or suppliers operating in the area, who are able to meet this service requirement.
The successful supplier will be expected to provide high-quality, fit-for-purpose products across an appropriate range of sizes, alongside reliable stock availability, delivery, returns and exchange arrangements. The procurement will seek to achieve value for money while ensuring appropriate safety, quality and service standards are maintained throughout the contract period.
Suppliers wishing to participate in this procurement must be registered on the Jaggaer eSourcing platform, through which the procurement opportunity and associated documentation will be managed. Suppliers who are not currently registered can register at Jaggaer eSourcing platform - https://beisgroup.ukp.app.jaggaer.com/. 
Suppliers must also be registered on the Central Digital Platform and have a valid Procurement Act 2023 unique organisation identifier, known as a PPON. Information on registration and obtaining a PPON can be found in the Central Digital Platform guidance - https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/faq/en_GB/Central_Digital_Platform . 
Suppliers interested in this opportunity should contact sourcing@gbe.gov.uk in advance of the market engagement session, which will take place on 1 December 2026. Requests to attend this session will close at 4pm on the 30/11/2026. Suppliers who register their interest and attend the market engagement session will subsequently be invited to tender for this requirement.

notices.title: Asbestos Collection

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Asbestos currently cannot be disposed of at any of our recycling centres in Essex. When an item containing asbestos is accidently put into a waste skip it contaminates the entire load. Last year 230 tonnes of asbestos was incorrectly taken to recycling centres. This led to service disruption, site closures and increased waste disposal costs for specialist handling.
For the last 10 years we have utilised a collection service for Asbestos, where members of the public can access the service via the ECC website, customers must go online and confirm the amount and type of asbestos they need to have collected. ECC collected approximately 11600kg from households via this service last year.
ECC has prepared a questionnaire (below) which invites providers to complete and submit. All information submitted will be treated in confidence and any references to the findings will be reported on a summary level on an anonymous basis. The purpose of this market engagement is to better understand the market’s appetite and capability in respect of a number of commercial topics.
NOTE: This premarket engagement notice is intended as an information gathering exercise. Participation in this survey is no indication of a commitment to participate in any future tendering process nor does it infer any preferential or special status on those individuals and organisations who participate.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
This notice is not a call for competition, does not constitute a tender or invitation to tender, and does not commit the Cabinet Office to run a procurement or award any contract.
The Cabinet Office intends to procure a robust, industry-standard Software as a Service (SaaS) Learning Management System (LMS) through the Government Commercial Agency  (GCA) RM6219 Learning and Training Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS), to support the new National School of Government and Public Services Learning & Development (L&D) offering.
The purpose of this notice is to invite suppliers on the DPS to review the high-level criteria outlined below and support the finalisation of the Statement of Requirements (SoR) by providing responses to key technical and operational questions.
The Cabinet Office anticipates that the LMS would need to support a user base of over 558,000 users and would be expected to meet security and information assurance requirements, including UK hosting of data and adherence to Secure by Design principles. All requirements are draft and may change.
Scope of Requirements
We are keen to hear from Suppliers who provide SaaS Learning Management Systems (LMS) and associated implementation and migration support services across the following areas:
Mandatory Requirements
Please note: The mandatory requirements must be met by all potential Suppliers. These mandatory requirements are subject to change following Market Engagement, and noting in this Notice constitutes a final specification.
● Security and Information Assurance: Mandatory UK hosting of data and adherence to 'Secure by Design' principles.
● Scalability and Accessibility: Platform capability to support over 558,000 users.
Essential Requirements
● Core LMS Capability: Learning catalogue, content tagging, search, and user interface.
● Booking and Administration: Booking and administration functionality across learning workflows.
● Admin Controls: End-to-end administration controls of central delivery offer and repository.
● Migration Support: Support for migration of existing catalogue of learning.
● Quality Data: Feedback mechanisms, advanced reporting, and evaluation metrics.
Out of Scope
We are currently not looking for Suppliers to provide L&D training content. The requirement is strictly for the provision of the LMS platform and associated implementation and support services; the platform will be used to host internally developed learning content.

notices.title: HAR6214 Victoria Park Lido

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
The London Borough of Tower Hamlets is seeking two appointments with regard to the delivery of a Lido in Victoria Park. This project is a Mayoral commitment and will provide an opportunity to improve access to swimming and support public health, enhance the borough’s leisure and cultural offer and increase the draw of Victoria Park as a regional destination. 
Both appointments will be procured through the Government Commercial Agency RM6356 Construction Professional Services 2 Framework, specifically Lot 1. 
The procurement will be split into two Lots as follows: 
Lot 1: Multidisciplinary Design Team (MDT). To procure and appoint a Multidisciplinary Design Team from RIBA Stage 0 to 3 (including planning application) to develop design proposals for Victoria Park Lido. The appointment will include a contract break clause at the end of RIBA Stage 1 to allow for review of the feasibility report and viability assessment. Upon a successful review the appointment will proceed with the same multidisciplinary team to carry out design development of RIBA stage 2 & 3 including the submission of the planning application.
Lot 2: Quantity Surveyor / Employers Agent. To procure and appoint a Quantity Surveyor / Employers Agent from RIBA Stage 0 to 7 (including the submission of the planning application) to develop design proposals for Victoria Park Lido. 
To maintain independence between the multidisciplinary design function and the independent Quantity Surveyor/ Employer’s Agent assurance role, bidders are not permitted to submit tenders for both Lots.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ABOUT FCC

FCC is Canada’s leading agriculture and food lender, dedicated to the industry that feeds the world. FCC employees are committed to the long-standing success of those who produce and process Canadian food by providing flexible financing, AgExpert business management software, information and knowledge. FCC provides a complement of expertise and services designed to support the complex and evolving needs of food businesses. As a financial Crown corporation, FCC is a stable partner that reinvests profits back into the industry and communities it serves. For more information, visit fcc.ca.

FCC complies with federal direction regarding procurement including requirements set forth by the Buy Canadian Framework. Information on the framework of polices may be found here: https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/buy-canadian-policy


RFP CONTACT

Lisa Achtemichuk
Strategic Sourcing Specialist
Farm Credit Canada
itprocurement@fcc.ca

RFP SCOPE

FCC is seeking a solution that enables the creation, modification, and production of AI-generated audio and video content for internal and external communications, marketing campaigns, awareness initiatives, and multimedia productions.
The proposed Platform should support the creation of high-quality, professional-grade audio and video content while minimizing manual effort and production timelines.
The proposed solution must be a commercially available, out-of-the-box (COTS) solution that is fully functional without the need for custom development, bespoke coding, or material modification to meet FCC's core business requirements. Proponents should demonstrate how their solution can efficiently execute post-production work to meet strategic video requests in a compressed turn around time.
The solution should enable FCC production teams to accelerate routine or time-sensitive production activities while maintaining appropriate control over content quality, branding and final outputs.

For further details, refer to the RFP and Appendix A (RFP Schedule, Evaluation Process, Scope and Proposal Instructions) documents that are uploaded to MERX.



RFP PARTICULARS
 

	All conditions for Proponent participation are included in the RFP documents.
	Duration of Contract: Up to 10 Years including option years.


RFP SCHEDULE
 

	RFP Release Date:  November 23, 2026
	Proponent Questions Accepted Until:  November 30, 2026 at 2:00PM*
	FCC Response to Proponent Questions Delivered Before:  December 14, 2026 at 5:00PM*
	RFP Closing Date/Time:  January 5, 2027 at 2:00PM*


NOTE: All times are CST – Saskatchewan. The above dates are subject to change at the sole discretion of FCC. Any changes to the RFP Schedule will be communicated to all Proponents via amendment on MERX.

RFP PROCESS CONSIDERATIONS
 

	This opportunity is covered under the provisions of Chapter 5 (Government Procurement) of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) and Chapter 19 (Government Procurement) of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and Canada-UK Trade Continuity Agreement (CUKTCA).

 


	This opportunity is subject to the Buy Canadian Policy Framework and open only to Canadian suppliers and suppliers located in the territory of an applicable trading partner.

 


	FCC is subject to the Official Languages Act (Canada). Proponents may choose to respond to this RFP in their official language of choice (English or French).

 


	This opportunity notice references a non-binding, competitive RFP, and is not a call for tenders. FCC is not obligated to proceed with the Work described in the RFP Scope, and may cancel the RFP at any time. FCC’s procurement process allows for consecutive or concurrent negotiations between FCC and one (1) or multiple Proponents, prior to awarding a Contract.


MERX ELECTRONIC BIDDING SYSTEM
 

	This Request for Proposals (RFP), including any attachments and amendments to such RFP, is available for download by the Proponent on MERX. MERX is a Canadian Public Tenders electronic bidding system accessible at https://www.merx.com. It is the sole responsibility of the Proponent to ensure its compatibility with MERX.
	Proponent proposals MUST be submitted electronically through MERX, preferably in a PDF or MS Word file, prior to the RFP Closing Date/Time specified in the RFP. Proposals submitted in other formats, by other methods or through any other means, or after the RFP Closing Date/Time specified in the RFP, may be rejected by FCC.



PRIORITY OF DOCUMENTS

In the event there are any discrepancies between this opportunity notice and the information on the MERX website proper, this opportunity notice shall take precedence.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
The objective of this requirement is to procure a cloud-based Software as a Service (SaaS)
Emergency Notification System (ENS) to support Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada's emergency
management, employee safety, business continuity, and incident communication requirements.
The system must enable authorized users to rapidly communicate emergency notifications and
operational alerts to employees, contractors, visitors, emergency management personnel, and
designated stakeholders during emergencies, incidents, exercises, and business continuity
events.
The solution must provide the following key capabilities:
1. Multi-channel emergency notification through SMS, voice calls, email, and desktop
notifications.
2. Targeted and mass notification capabilities for specific groups, facilities, regions, or all
AAFC personnel.
3. Real-time accountability and response management functions that allow recipients to
acknowledge notifications and provide status updates.
4. Support for emergency exercises, business continuity events, operational disruptions,
severe weather events, security incidents, and other emergencies.
5. Secure, reliable, and highly available communication capabilities during emergency
situations.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Advance Procurement Notice

Inspection, Testing and Maintenance (ITM) and minor repair services of HVAC and chiller mechanical systems
CFB Kingston, Ontario
(with Security Requirements)

1. Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Kingston, Ontario.

The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

2. Description of the Project and Services
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.
APN Number: 85856
Approximate Estimate: $1,580,000, up to $3,950,000
Anticipated Posting: February 2027

Description:
Contractor services and deliverables required for the Inspection, Testing and Minor Repair of various chiller systems, air handling units and other HVAC items associated with facility infrastructure at Canadian Forces Base Kingston, including the Royal Military College (RMC), Fort Frontenac, and the Kingston and Brockville Armouries.

The contract will include but is not limited to: Scheduled Inspection, Testing and Minor Repairs of various HVAC equipment (Condensing Units, Air Handling Units, and Exhaust Fans) as well as Daikin, Smardt, Trane and McQuay brand name Chillers. Work shall be performed in accordance with manufacturer recommendations, applicable codes, environmental regulations, and industry best practices.
The contractor’s services will entail scheduled preventive maintenance, seasonal start-up and shutdown procedures, operational inspections, performance testing, refrigerant management, control system verification, condition reporting, and emergency response support. The contractor shall identify deficiencies, recommend corrective actions, and perform authorized repairs to minimize downtime and extend equipment service life.

This contract is expected to be awarded to one (1) firm for two (2) years with an option to add up to three additional, one (1) year extensions. The estimated services are expected to cost $790,000 per year for a contract value of $1,580,000 with possibility to extend up to a total amount of $3,950,000.

3. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements
To be eligible for contract award, a tenderers will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.
The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of Secret.

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a tender for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.
Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.
To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.
In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.

5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.
Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor:

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and
	has submitted a bid

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Contractors that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:
Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:
Robin Entwistle
Team Leader, Contract Services
Defence Construction Canada
613-449-4964
KNContracting@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the bidder or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated  sponsorship process.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is calling for abbreviated proposals from consulting firms to award TWO (2) Standing Offer Agreements (SOA) to provide “as and when required” the following professional services at St-Jean Garrison and Montréal Garrison, and their satellite sites.

	preparation of a Statement of Requirement and concept, design development, construction documents, assistance during the tender call, construction phases and any necessary architectural services for the construction of the new or renovation of the existing building.

Information provided by the Proponents will be evaluated using the established criteria in the RFAP. The objective of this RFAP is to select the two proponents with the highest total score.

Each SOA will be for a period of one (1) year with a maximum estimated value of $ 500,000.00. If mutually agreeable between the Consultant and DCC, each SOA may be extended for up to two (2) additional one-year period and increased in the order of $500,000.00 two times. Call-ups under the SOA are expected to be valued between $ 20,000.00 and $ 80,000.00; the maximum value of a call-up under the SOA is $ 100,000.00. Refer to the RFAP document for additional information.

This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Chapter Nineteen of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA).

Firms that consider themselves qualified to provide these services are invited to submit their Abbreviated Proposals through the MERX Electronic Bidding System on or before the closing date and time indicated on the Electronic Bidding System.

The selected consultant will be required to hold a valid DOS, issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).  Details concerning the Security Requirements for this project are identified in the RFAP documents.
Questions regarding this solicitation are to be directed ONLY to the point of contact identified in this advertisement.  Proponents who address their questions to anyone other than the point of contact during the solicitation period may, for that reason alone, be disqualified.
Please note that the preliminary results for this solicitation will be available on MERX.

Proponents can obtain contract award results from the DCC Website at Contract Activity - Defence Construction Canada (dcc-cdc.gc.ca)

Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for New CADSS/MAJAID Facility

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – TRS18081_73944 – New CADSS/MAJAID Facility, Trenton, Ontario

Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary to build a new warehouse and operations facility to support the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit.

This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered.
Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase.

DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI.

As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase.
This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA).

1. Project background
The CADSS/MAJAID Facility project at 8 Wing CFB Trenton consists of the construction of a new 1,554 m² warehouse and operations facility to support the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit. The work comprises general contracting services and the supply and installation of all labour and materials required to construct the facility, including associated building systems and site infrastructure. The facility will provide space for parachute inspection, drying, preparation, and packing activities, while also accommodating administrative functions, operational storage requirements, and material handling activities.

The proposed facility includes a dedicated carpentry shop, warehouse storage areas, administrative office space, and specialized infrastructure to support operational equipment and warehouse activities involving forklifts and other machinery. Key features include storage and racking systems, a 20-tonne overhead bridge crane, and a parachute drying tower.

The facility includes a steel-framed structure enclosed with prefinished metal cladding and high-performance insulated wall assemblies. The roofing system consists of a steel deck structure with a two-ply modified bitumen membrane and insulated roof assembly. Mechanical systems include plumbing, sanitary and storm drainage, natural gas distribution, compressed air, HVAC, make-up air units, ventilation systems, heat recovery, dust collection, and building controls. Fire protection and life-safety systems include a wet-pipe sprinkler system, fire alarm system, fire department connection, emergency lighting, exit signage, and associated monitoring and control equipment. Site works include new water, sanitary, storm, electrical, communications, and site power services, including a new 300 kVA pad-mounted transformer, underground electrical distribution, communications duct banks, parking receptacles, and utility connections to support facility operations. Exterior site development also includes landscaping and paving requirements, including paved areas to support vehicle access, parking, loading, and facility operations, together with associated site restoration and landscaping. The project will meet all applicable codes and standards.

2. Documents
Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage.
Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5.

3.Estimate
The Rough Order Magnitude estimate for this Contract is $12.5 Million (Current Year $).
This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies.

4. Schedule
DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around January 2027.
The works shall reach substantial completion no later than 420 calendar days following the notification of contract award and shall be completed no later than 35 calendar days after the substantial completion date.

5. Site visit
No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit.

6. Access to information Act
Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act.

7. Questions and clarifications
Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System.

DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer.

In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System.

8. Language of the Tender and the contract 
By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract.
In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System.
Unless otherwise specified in the Contract, all Contract Documents to which the Contract applies or refers, as well as all deliverables, documents, reports and results of the work, services or goods that the Contractor submits, provides, or delivers to DCC or Canada in connection with the performance of the Contract, shall be in the language chosen by the Contractor on the Electronic Bid System.

9. Joint venture A joint venture is an association of two or more parties that pools their funds, assets, knowledge, expertise, or other resources into a joint business venture, sometimes called a consortium, to bid together for a requirement. Tenderers submitting interest as a joint venture will be required to clearly indicate in the Electronic Submission System that they are forming a joint venture and should provide the following information:

	the name of the joint venture, if applicable,
	the name of the representative of the joint venture, i.e., the member chosen by the other members to represent them, if applicable,
	the name of each member of the joint venture

10. Security Requirements During Construction
The Contractor will be required to hold, at all times during the performance of the construction contract, at least a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) issued by Public Services and Procurement Canada's (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). In the case of a joint venture, all parties to the joint venture must hold at least a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

DCC has issued an Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number TRS18081_73944 to allow contractors that do not hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) security clearance to initiate the sponsorship process prior to the launch of the tender phase. For information on the sponsorship process, consult the APN on MERX or visit https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.
To be eligible to participate in the tender phase, a Tenderer who does not hold a valid Designated Organization Verification (DOS) security clearance will be required to:

	have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Tender phase (second step Tender Phase) as indicated in the Electronic Bidding System (MERX);
	meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the tender call (Tender phase) as indicated in the Electronic Bidding System (MERX); and
	Have submitted a response to this RFEOI.

” sponsorship application” means the activity of having completed the questionnaire on the DCC web page and having forwarded the answers to the DCC Industrial Security Program (ISP)”.
” sponsorship application package” means the activity of completing and forwarding the following forms to the DCC Industrial Security Program (ISP): the Application for Registration (AFR) for Canadian legal entities form, the Company Security Officer form, the Security Agreement form, the Security Clearance form, the Fingerprints Applicant form, the Alternate Company Security form and the Personnel Screening form”.
Failure to comply with these requirements will result in a tenderer not being allowed to participate in the tender phase. However, if DCC determines, in its sole discretion that the tenderer could not comply with these requirements because of an undue administrative delay on the part of CSP or DCC, DCC may, in its sole discretion, allow the tenderer to participate in the tender phase.

11. Closing location
Responses to this RFEOI must be received through the Electronic Bidding System.  Responses sent by fax, mail or email will not be accepted.

12. Closing Date and Time
The closing date and time indicated in the Electronic Submission System will be the official closing date and time of this RFEOI.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Advance Procurement Notice

Facilities Maintenance & Support Services
CFB Kingston, Ontario
(with Security Requirements)

1. Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform Facility Maintenance Contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Kingston.

The purpose of this APN is to allow Facility Maintenance Contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.
This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Facility Maintenance Contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

2. Description of the Project and Services
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN Number:   87829
Approximate Estimate:  $40,000,000 for a period of 5 years, with 6 optional years estimated at $8M/year. Total opportunity of approximately $90M over 11 years.
Anticipated Posting: February 2027

Description:
The Facility Maintenance Services Contract will require multi-trade and single trade contractors to provide services for approximately 130 buildings of varying size and complexity across 6 sites under Real Property Operations (RP Ops) Det Kingston. The majority of the buildings are within Kingston city limits, with 1 Armoury located in Brockville, ON and 1 Armoury located in Cornwall, ON.

Description of Services:
The Contract will consist of facilities management and maintenance services that include inspection, testing, maintenance, and repairs of equipment and systems, such as HVACR, electrical, plumbing, fire detection and suppression, elevators and lifting systems, overhead cranes and vehicle hoists, backflow preventers, hydrants, security and access control, overhead doors, generators & UPS, pool systems, fume hoods, life safety systems, fuel storage tanks, roads, concrete sidewalks/curbs, fencing, as well as architectural elements such as roofs and interior repairs.

3. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements
To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is FACILITY SECURITY CLEARANCE (FSC) at the level of SECRET.

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.
In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.

5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor:

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and
	has submitted a proposal.  

DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:
Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:
Robin Entwistle
Team Leader, Contract Services
Defence Construction Canada
613-449-4964
KNContracting@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

notices.title: Stage 2 - Water Treatment Plant System Upgrade, Riding Mountain National Park

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
REQUIREMENT

Parks Canada requires a qualified General Contractor to complete construction-phase upgrades to the Water Treatment Plant control system at Riding Mountain National Park. The work includes upgrading the existing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) and Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) systems, together with associated hardware, software, control panels, communications, electrical connections, operator interfaces, and field-device integration.

The Construction Contractor will supply and install the required equipment; develop or modify PLC and SCADA programming; integrate the upgraded system with existing plant processes and instrumentation; complete testing, start-up, commissioning, operator training, and closeout documentation; and correct deficiencies. All work must be coordinated with Parks Canada and plant operators to maintain safe and continuous water-treatment operations. Planned shutdowns, system cutovers, and temporary control arrangements require prior approval.

TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS 

This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings.

Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid.

Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

sections.text:
DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) is requesting Proposals from Design-Build Teams to design and construct the new of Combined Joint Intelligence Modernization (CJIM) Joint Intelligence Training Centre (JITC) at CFB Kingston following a modified design-build approach. Additional details are provided in the Request for Proposals (RFP) documents.

The estimated cost for this opportunity is in the range of $26.7M

Firms that consider themselves qualified to provide these services are invited to submit their proposals through the MERX Electronic Bidding System on or before the closing date and time indicated on the Electronic Bidding System.
This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Chapter Nineteen of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA).

The selected contractor will be required to hold a valid Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET and obtain approved Document Safeguarding Capability at the level of SECRET, issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).  Details concerning the Security Requirements for this project are identified in Amendment No.1 to the solicitation documents.

Questions regarding this solicitation are to be directed ONLY to the point of contact identified in this advertisement.  Bidders who address their questions to anyone other than the point of contact during the solicitation period may, for that reason alone, be disqualified.
Bidders can obtain contract award results from the DCC website at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/contract-activity.

DCC now publicly discloses information on payments made to prime contractors so that subcontractors know when they can expect payment. Information on payments made in the past 90 days on construction contracts over $100,000, as well as further information regarding DCC’s prompt payment commitment, can be obtained from the DCC website at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/contract-activity.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Maintenance and Storage Hangar Facility (Modified Design-Build)
Ottawa, Ontario
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform design-builders of an upcoming contract opportunity in Ottawa, Ontario.

The purpose of this APN is to allow design-builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested design-builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

Contract Number: 87755
Approximate Estimate: $180M-$220M
Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027

This project involves the design and construction of a purpose-built maintenance and storage hangar facility in the Ottawa region. The new building will provide modern, secure, and efficient infrastructure to support aircraft storage, inspection, maintenance, and operational readiness. The project will include the full design of the facility, site development, and construction of hangar bays, maintenance spaces, and associated support and operational areas. Additional scope may also be added through change order.

The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract. The estimated construction design and construction cost of this project is in the range of $180M–$220M (subject to further definition) whereas the additional potential scope is estimated at $120M (subject to analysis, definition and approvals). It is anticipated that this solicitation may be initiated in Winter 2027, conditional upon project approvals and funding authorization.

The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project.

To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the MDB contracts. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities.

3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of Secret.

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.

5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builders:

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and
	has submitted a proposal.  

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Design-Builders that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent  regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:

Priscille Vumi
Leader, Contract Services
Defence Construction Canada
343-596-6289
priscille.vumi@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the  proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Maintenance and repair of manufacturing machinery, tools and equipment for CORCAN

This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, CORCAN Atlantic region.

Trade agreement:

Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: 

This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner.

Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid.

Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: 

This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers.

Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement:

This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement.

Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements.

Nature of Requirements: 

The following is a summary of the Statement of Work for this requirement. 

The Correctional Service Canada (CSC), CORCAN in the Atlantic region, is seeking a qualified Contractor to provide professional mechanical services for the repair and maintenance of its equipment in different manufacturing sites in the provinces of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia.

Objectives: The Contractor must perform preventative maintenance and repair on tools, machinery and different equipment at various manufacturing sites in the Atlantic Region.

Deliverables: 

The Contractor’s Technical Resource must perform the work at various CSC locations in the Atlantic Region as listed below:

Community Industries Moncton – 310 Baig boulevard, Moncton, New Brunswick
Dorchester Penitentiary – 4902 Main Street, Dorchester, New Brunswick
Springhill Institution – 330 McGee Street, Springhill, Nova Scotia

1.	The Contractor must provide the Project Authority:

a.	A monthly report that includes the following as a minimum: 
i.	the date at which the Contractor performed the work; 
ii.	the Work Site where the work was completed;
iii.	a brief description of the preventative maintenance and repair services performed, including the tools, machinery, or equipment serviced, and the work completed;
iv.	The total time spent maintaining and repairing each tool, machinery, equipment.

2.	The Technical Resource (technician) must:
 
a.	Perform maintenance, repairs, installation and relocation of CORCAN tools, machinery and equipment according to the schedule of tasks to be performed. 
 
b.	Complete a time sheet and obtain approval from a CORCAN Shop Supervisor on site at the end of each workday or service call.

c.	Provide the CORCAN official on site with a service report before leaving the site. The service report must identify the tool, machinery, or equipment serviced and document the work performed, findings, test results, parts installed or recommended, any outstanding efficiencies, and the operational status of the asset. The Technical Resource must leave a copy of the service report on site and provide the original to the on-site Production Supervisor, Shop Instructor or Operations Manager upon request.

d.	Prepare and submit a schedule of planned tasks for the following week to the CORCAN Shop Supervisor each Friday.

Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none.

Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment.

Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: 

Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of February 1, 2027, to January 31, 2028 with the option to renew for three (3) additional one-year periods.

File Number: 21C20-26-5334179

Contracting Authority: Karine Clément
Telephone number: 450-506-3180
E-mail: karine.clement@csc-scc.gc.ca

The Crown reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement.

Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada (English or French).

After contract award, bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. notices.title: TBIPS SA - I.9. System Administrator and I.10. Technical Architect

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
The Office of the Secretary to the Governor General (OSGG) Information Technology Directorate is responsible for all information technology systems, including their deployment, maintenance and support. These systems include, but are not limited to, servers, desktops, applications, networks, messaging, virtualization, security, storage, authentication services, Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) and cloud computing/networking.

While the OSGG IT Directorate provides day-to-day operational support for the IT environment, certain requirements involving high-priority incidents, complex infrastructure issues, specialized technical expertise, or time-limited initiatives exceed the capacity or expertise available internally.

The OSGG requires access to a flexible source of specialized technical expertise, on an as-requested basis through Task Authorizations, to support the resolution of priority incidents, infrastructure and cloud initiatives, system optimization activities, technical planning, architecture services, documentation, and knowledge transfer requirements.

Canada may require a team of up to five (5) resources under the following TBIPS resource categories:

Two (2) I.9 System Administrator (Level 3) resources; and
Three (3) I.10 Technical Architect (Level 3) resources.

Services may involve network, infrastructure, cloud, storage, security and related technologies within the OSGG environment and will be performed through Task Authorizations issued on an as-and-when-requested basis.

notices.title: ACAN - Preventative Maintenance for Orbitrap ID-X Mass Spectrometer and Ultra-high performance liquid chromatograph (UHPLC) Instruments

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
1.	Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN)

An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada intends to award a contract for services to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the Contracting Authority may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier.

2.	Definition of the requirement

The Department of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada has a requirement for Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. to provide preventative maintenance services for one (1) Orbitrap ID-X, IC Ready Mass Spectrometer (Serial Number FSN30102) connected with Vanquish Binary Pump, Vanquish Split Sampler FT, and Vanquish Column Compartment H located at the Morden Research and Development Centre. 

The service will involve the following under an Essential Support Plan: 
-	Field Service Engineer labor, travel, and parts required for any unlimited Corrective Maintenance visits within a 72h response time.
-	Technical Support inquiries with a targeted immediate response time provided by a certified service engineer using the latest digital remote support tools. 
-	One (1) scheduled annual standard Preventive Maintenance visit including replacement parts (Standard PM Kit included).
-	Instrument Requalification (RQ) in conjunction with a scheduled Corrective Maintenance with a purchase of an add-on Operational Qualification. 
-	Access to Unity Lab Services Online Knowledge Base subscription. 
-	Software and firmware updates upon request and in conjunction with a scheduled Preventative Maintenance or Corrective Maintenance visit. 
-	10% discount on spare parts not covered by Corrective Maintenance, and accessories and consumables for the instruments, and 10% discounts off list price for any training classes purchased during the contract period. 

3.	Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements)

Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: 
-	Are an authorized vendor who are certified and authorized to maintain and repair Orbitrap ID-X Mass Spectrometers and UHPLC Instruments to restore instruments operating as intended. 

4.	Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement

This procurement is subject to the following trade agreement(s):
?	Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA)
?	Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA)
?	Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement
?	Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement
?	Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement 
?	Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement
?	Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA)

5.	Justification for the Pre-Identified Supplier

Thermo Fisher Scientific owns the design of this equipment.  There is no other company that can provide parts, training, service or repairs because the architecture and technology belong to Thermo Fisher Scientific.  Since Thermo Fisher is the original manufacturer of this equipment, they are the only company that have trained service engineers that are qualified to do the trouble shooting and repairs on their technology should something break down.

6.	Government Contracts Regulations Exception(s)

The following exception(s) to the Government Contracts Regulations is invoked for this procurement under subsection. 

 6.(d) - "only one person or firm is capable of performing the work".

Where, for works of art, or for reasons connected with the protection of patents, copyrights or other exclusive rights, or proprietary information or where there is an absence of competition for technical reasons, the goods or services can be supplied only by a particular supplier and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists.

7.	Exclusions and/or Limited Tendering Reasons

The following exclusion(s) and/or limited tendering reasons are invoked under the:

?	Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) – Article(s) 513 (b) ii
?	Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) – Article(s) Kbis-09 (b)
?	Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement – Article(s) 1409 1. (b)
?	Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement – Article(s) 17.11 (b) (i) 
?	Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement – referencing the WTO Protocol Amending the GPA, Article XIII (1) (b)
?	Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement – Article(s) 16.10 (b) (ii)
?	Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) – Article(s) 1409 (b) (ii)

8.	Period of the proposed contract

The proposed contract is for a period of 3 years, from estimated start date: January 15, 2027 to estimated completion date: January 14, 2030. 

9.	Cost estimate of the proposed contract

The estimated value of the contract is $ 223,853.05 (including all applicable taxes).

10.	Name and address of the pre-identified supplier

Thermo Fisher Scientific (Mississauga) Inc. 
4-2845 Argentia Road
MISSISSAUGA, ON  L5N 8G6

11.	Suppliers' right to submit a statement of capabilities

Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to provide the services described in the ACAN may submit a statement of capabilities in writing by Email to the Contracting Authority identified in this notice on or before the closing date of this notice. The statement of capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements.

12.	Closing date for a submission of a statement of capabilities.

The closing date and time for accepting statements of capabilities is December 1 at 11:00 a.m., CST.

13.	Inquiries and statements of capabilities are to be directed to:

Melissa Smith
Procurement Specialist
Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada
Western Service Centre
Telephone: 306-515-4796
Email address: melissa.smith3@agr.gc.ca

Please note that the Department of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada will not accept hard copy submissions. Email submissions must be less than 20 MB; if the file(s) are larger please split them into more than one email. Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. The Department is not responsible for misdirected or delayed submissions. All submissions must be received by the closing date and time specified above.

All submissions should note the following file number in the subject line of the e-mail: # 
WSC-2627-200

Statement of Capabilities received on or before the closing date will be considered solely for the purpose of deciding whether or not to conduct a competitive procurement. Information provided will be used by AAFC for technical evaluation purposes only, and will not to be construed as a proposal. Your written Statement of Capabilities must provide sufficient evidence that demonstrates it is capable of fulfilling AAFCs requirement. Suppliers who submit a Statement of Capabilities prior to the closing date and time will be notified in writing as to the Department’s decision whether it will continue with the aforementioned procurement, or proceed to a full bid solicitation process.

If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the fifteen (15) calendar day posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, the government will proceed to a full tendering process on either the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the contract.

If no other supplier submits, on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a contract will be awarded to the preselected supplier.

sections.text:
DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) is requesting proposals from firms with demonstrated experience in the Construction Management at Risk (CMAR) delivery method, to submit a Proposal for a Program involving multiple Projects for the recapitalization of the John Foote Armoury in Hamilton, Ontario.

Notwithstanding that the Program comprises multiple Projects, a single CCDC 5B Construction Management Contract – for Services and Construction will govern the entirety of the Program for the full duration of the Contract.

The Construction Manager will be required to provide the necessary Construction Management services to ensure the successful completion of all Projects under the Program. These services apply to all construction activities associated with the Projects, are divided into two (2) components and include, but are not limited to, the following:

	Pre-construction Services: General Services, Pre-design, Schematic Design, Design Development, Construction Document, and Construction Procurement.
	Construction Services: General Services, Cost Control and Accounting, and Post-Construction Services.

Additional details are provided in the RFP document.

The resulting Contract will include an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) that aims to provide opportunities for businesses owned and lead by Indigenous People. Canada’s free trade agreements pose no impediment to the inclusion of measures for the benefit of Indigenous Peoples and/or businesses in a procurement. Refer to the RFP documents for more details.

You may consult the Indigenous Services Canada’s business directory, and/or Canadian Council for Indigenous Business’ directory as required.

A site visit has been arranged for the following date, time, and location.  It is highly recommended that bidders attend this visit.
Date: November 23, 2026
Time: 10:00 AM local time
Location: 200 James St N, Hamilton, Ontario.

Site visit attendees will be required to sign in at the Commissionaires booth where a government issued piece of identification is required. Please allow enough time to sign in as the site visit will start promptly at 10a.m. (estimated site visitation duration is 2 hours). Please note that there is no on-site parking available.

The estimated construction cost for the Program is in the range of $110 Million.

Firms that consider themselves qualified to provide these services are invited to submit their proposals through the MERX Electronic Bidding System on or before the closing date and time indicated on the Electronic Bidding System.

This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Chapter Nineteen of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA).

The selected Construction Manager will be required to hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS), issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).  Details concerning the Security Requirements for this program are identified in the RFP documents.

Questions regarding this solicitation are to be directed ONLY to the point of contact identified in this advertisement.  Bidders who address their questions to anyone other than the point of contact during the solicitation period may, for that reason alone, be disqualified.

Bidders can obtain contract award results from the DCC website at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/contract-activity.

DCC now publicly discloses information on payments made to prime contractors so that subcontractors know when they can expect payment. Information on payments made in the past 90 days on construction contracts over $100,000, as well as further information regarding DCC’s prompt payment commitment, can be obtained from the DCC website at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/contract-activity.

The Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (IAAC) requires Stream 4 - Geospatial Informatics Services, under the Solutions Based Informatics Professional Services supply arrangement, on an as-and-when-required basis to support the operation, maintenance, enhancement, modernization, and sustainability of its enterprise Geographic Information System (GIS) environment.

The Contractor shall provide senior-level geospatial informatics professional services related to enterprise GIS architecture, GIS application development, data management and integration, GIS platform modernization, and the assessment and implementation of emerging geospatial technologies, including artificial intelligence-enabled capabilities.

Services may include strategic, business, technical, and architectural advisory services; the preparation of recommendations, plans, standards, and guidance; and support for the design, development, implementation, maintenance, optimization, and migration of enterprise GIS applications, data, services, and infrastructure, including environments managed in accordance with Shared Services Canada (SSC) requirements and applicable Government of Canada standards.

The Department of National Defence requires the following items:

Quantity 1 Charpy test machine with additional accessories and software as described in the RFP.

Requirement: to replace an obsolete Charpy machine. A Charpy Impact Test Machine is a laboratory testing instrument used to determine the impact toughness and fracture resistance of metallic and other engineering materials. The machine measures the amount of energy absorbed by a standardized notched test specimen when it is struck by a pendulum hammer under controlled conditions.

Requested delivery date for all of the above mentioned is March 15th 2027

Goods must be consigned and delivered to QETE Supply Warehouse, NPB Building, 45 Blvd Sacré Coeur, Room C1113, Ramp 7, Gatineau, QC, J8X 1C6.

notices.title: NPP - Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Trade Agreement: CFTA, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Colombia Free Trade agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement.

Tendering Procedures: to all pre-qualified suppliers under the Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI under Crystallography Equipment.

Competitive Procurement Strategy: Lowest cost

Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: No

Nature of Requirements: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector 

THIS REQUEST IS RESERVED FOR HOLDERS OF SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT # E60PV-19EQUI ONLY, FOR THE PURCHASE OF LABORATORY AND SCIENTIFIC EQUIPMENT, PARTS AND ACCESSORIES, SERVICES AND SUPPLIES.

Only Suppliers currently pre-qualified on Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI have been invited to bid.

As a requirement of the Supply Arrangement, this notice is published on Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) for a period of 40 calendar days. The closing date published on this notice identifies how long the notice will be published. For the closing date of any solicitation under the supply arrangement, invited suppliers should refer to the solicitation documents. 

Suppliers that do not have a Supply Arrangement for the supply of Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies with Public Works and Government Services Canada, cannot submit a bid. Any bids received from suppliers not pre-qualified on the Supply Arrangement will not be evaluated.

Suppliers may qualify under Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI for Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies, at any time. Interested suppliers should download solicitation document E60PV-19EQUI/D from CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba) and submit a response as per the requirements of the Request for Supply Arrangement.


Item : Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector 
Quantity: 1

  The mandatory technical criteria are: 	

#	MANDATORY TECHNICAL CRITERIA	
M1   Must be capable of being installed on a TESCAN Mira3 XMH model scanning electron microscope	
M2	Must come equipped with a CMOS sensor, a phosphor screen, and fibre-optic coupling	
M3	Must be capable of collecting EBSD patterns with image sizes up to 1244x1024	
M4	Must have pattern acquisition speeds of up to 5700 patterns per second at 156x128 resolution	
M5	Must allow analyses at beam currents as low as 400 pA and accelerating voltages as low as 5kV	
M6	Must be capable of angular resolution up to 0.05 degrees	
M7	Must have motorized screen elevation control and insertion/retraction control	
M8	Must come equipped with a 5 diode forescatter diode (FSD) array for orientation contrast, topographic contrast, and atomic number contrast imaging	
M9	Must come with a Windows PC workstation installed with software for data acquisition and processing.	
M10 Must be capable of simultaneous EDS/EBSD mapping with an X-Max 80 model EDS detector, permitting refined phase identification using sample chemistry.
Note: The X-Max 80 is the exact model of EDS detector currently installed in the laboratory. We rely on a function where simultaneously collected EDS data is used to aid in the correct identification of crystallographically similar phases during automated EBSD analyses, and therefore any new EBSD detector must be compatible with our X-Max 80.
