notices.title: APN_Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3, CFB Borden ON

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3
CFB Borden, Ontario
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Borden, Ontario.

The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES
It is anticipated that the following 2-Step (Step 1: Request for Expression of Interest, Step 2: Tender Phase) solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN Number: 88280
Approximate Estimate: $168 million for both buildings
Anticipated Posting Step 1: January 2027
Anticipated Posting Step 2: February 2027

Description:
The project comprises the construction of two new five-storey training quarters buildings at CFB Borden, Ontario. The buildings will use a site-adapted design based on the existing Training Quarters Building S-166.

The anticipated work includes building construction, mechanical and electrical systems, associated site development and connections to site services. The design will incorporate site-specific requirements and lessons learned from the existing building.

 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer or proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security screening requirement for each construction contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors or consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors or consultants that intend to submit a tender or a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers or proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors or consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.


5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors or consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor or consultant:

	Have submitted a response to the Step 1: RFEOI,
	have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Step 2: Tender Phase,
	meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the Step 2: Tender Phase, and
	Have submitted a tender to the Step 2: Tender Phase.

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Contractors or Consultants that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer or proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:

Victor Shekofteh
Contract Coordinator
Defence Construction Canada
249-535-4651
victor.shekofteh@dcc-cdc.gc.ca


7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer or proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Non-Hazardous Waste Removal

This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Grand Valley Institution, Kitchener, Ontario.

Trade agreement:	 Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Canada Korea Trade Agreement (CKTA)

Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: 

This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner.

Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid.

Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: 
This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers.

Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: 
This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement.

Security Requirements: 
This contract does not include security requirements.

Nature of Requirements: 

The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. 

The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) requires a contractor to provide the collection and disposal of non-hazardous waste, including recyclable and organic materials, at Grand Valley Institution. The contractor must provide all labour, materials, equipment, transportation, and bin rentals required to perform these services in accordance with applicable provincial regulations and landfill policies.

Deliverables: 

The Contractor must:

a)	Supply two (2) eight (8) cubic yard containers for Non-Hazardous Solid Waste at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 
b)	Supply one (1) eight (8) cubic yard container for Recyclable Cardboard at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 
c)	Supply ten (10) point ninety-six (96) gallon roll-out carts for Recyclable Glass and Plastic Co-Mingled at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 
d)	Supply six (6) thirty-two (32) gallon roll-out bins for Organic Waste at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 

e)	Supply one (1) four (4) cubic yard container for non-hazardous solid waste at 520 Manitou Drive. 
f)	Supply one (1) four (4) cubic yard container for cardboard at 520 Manitou Drive.
g)	Supply five (5) ninety-six (96) cubic yard roll-out carts for recyclable glass and plastic co-mingled at 520 Manitou Drive.
h)	Supply two (2) thirty-two (32) gallon roll-out bins for Organic Waste at 520 Manitou Drive.


i)	Maintain the cleanliness and appearance of bins always provided in good order.
j)	Pick-up Non-Hazardous Waste three (3) times per week (Monday, Wednesday & Friday), with the exception of Statutory Holidays. 
k)	Pick-up Cardboard Recyclables once a week, with the exception of Statutory Holidays. 
l)	Pick-up Co-Mingled Recyclables once a week, with the exception of Statutory Holidays.
m)	Pick-up Organic Waste once a week, with the exception of Statutory Holidays.
n)	Supply of all labour, materials and equipment necessary to collect, transport and properly dispose of the waste in accordance with Provincial/Federal/Municipal laws. 
o)	Provide lift weights for each stream of waste, recyclables and organics 
p)	Assume the responsibility for all waste, recyclables and organics after removal from the site.
q)	Provide weight verification slips from the landfill site, if requested, to support invoiced amounts. 


Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none.

Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment.

Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: 

Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2030. 

File Number: 21465-31-5487863

Contracting Authority: Robin Riha
Telephone number: 613-650-1203
E-mail: robin.riha@csc-scc.gc.ca

notices.title: Integrated Correctional program Model (ICPM) Program

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier.

1. Definition of the requirement:

Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement.

The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement for the delivery of programs to offenders.  The main goal of maintenance is to review and refine core self management skills and apply them to real-life situations, obstacles, and high-risk situations to reduce risk to re-offend. One Integrated Correctional program Model (ICPM) program cycle is delivered at a rate of one session per week for 12 weeks on a continuous intake basis. The work will involve the following:

1.1	Objectives:

To deliver ICPM to offenders.

1.2 Tasks:

The Contractor’s facilitator must:

a)	Obtains CSC’s Certification through the Quality Review process.
b)	Provide delivery of the requested number of ICPM sessions to offenders referred by CSC, depending upon the need and according to national directives, policy and guidelines to a maximum of 10 offenders;  
c)	Adhere to the course content by delivering program sessions for the ICPM Community Maintenance Programs in accordance with the program manual.
d)	Provide classroom space, program equipment and supplies, and all administrative services associated with the project;
e)	For all offenders who meet the criteria for enrollment to the ICPM Maintenance (MT) - the facilitator(s) must:
•	conduct file review;
•	complete pre-program semi-structured interview and interview booklet, return interview booklet to CSC; 
•	complete Pre and Post program testing and assessment interviews and enter the information into Offender Management System (OMS) under Generic Program Performance Measure (GPPM) Screen within the first two sessions;
•	ensure offenders understanding and signing (or refusal to sign) of program consent form prior to program commencement while documenting such in a casework record in OMS. The consent to participate form must be placed on the Education and Training File; 
•	prepare offender progress reports following the ICPM report template and enter the report into OMS at the completion of the required number of sessions;
•	forward all reports for review and approval by the Departmental Representative; 
•	review the report with the participant and document same in casework record;
•	return interview booklets to CSC 
f)	As per most recent Commissioner's Directive 726 - Correctional Programs, the facilitator must complete a casework record in OMS (unless at a site where there is no connectivity) within 1 working day:
•	when there is an offender contact which is not a requirement of the program,
•	an individual interview is completed with the offender,
•	a make-up session has been completed,
•	there is sharing of information regarding offender participation in the program,
•	after every session during the offenders’ cycle,
•	if there is significant information for the Case Management Team. Significant information would include but is not limited to the following: Breach of a condition, new offence, harm to self, harm to others, personal problems that impact risk.
g)	Each session must follow the same process (see below), be 2 hours in duration and includes a break of up to 15 minutes:
•	Roundtable and introductions (30 minutes)
•	Structured segment, each focusing on a specific theme and skills set (50 - 60 minutes)
•	Alternate Session – An alternate session may be offered in place of a structured segment session based on the identified needs of the participants present for that session, provided that the session is selected from pre-established topics within the program manual (PG 60 in ICPM Manual). 
•	Update Self-Management Plan (10 minutes)
•	Wrap-up (5 - 10 minutes)
h)	Programs are to be delivered Monday to Friday in the evenings between 6pm-8pm.

1.3	Training Requirements

The Contractor must participate in CSC-funded ICPM program delivery training when required and made available by CSC.
•	Training is delivered in person by CSC at the Correctional Learning and Development Centre in Moncton, New Brunswick.
•	Training dates are established by CSC based on operational requirements and the number of referrals identified by the Project Authority.
•	Initial training for CMP-MT consists of: 
 o	10 business days of initial program delivery training;
 o	2 days of Indigenous Social History training; and
 o	7.5 hours of Generic Program Performance Measure (GPPM) training delivered over 2 days.
•	The Contractor must also attend refresher training when significant changes are made to the program model or when requested by the Project Authority.
•	The Contractor will be reimbursed for authorized travel costs associated with training.
•	The Contractor will not be compensated for time spent attending training.

1.4 Performance standards:

Delivery of the ICPM: Community Maintenance Programs must be provided in accordance with the following documents:
•	Correctional Programs (CD 726);
•	National Correctional Program Standards (CD 726-1);
•	ICPM: Program Implementation and Program Management Guidelines
•	Commissioner’s Directives available at:
  •	English: http://www.csc-s.gc.ca/text/legislat_e.shtml
  •	French: http://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/text/legislat_f.shtml 
•	ICPM Community Maintenance Program (Multi Target) Manuals - when connected to OMS;

1.5		Paper consumption: 

a.	Should printed material be required, double sided printing in black and white format is the default unless otherwise specified by the Project Authority. 
b.	The Contractor must ensure printed material is on paper with a minimum recycled content of 30% and/or certified as originating from a sustainably managed forest. 
c.	The Contractor must recycle unneeded printed documents (in accordance with Security Requirements).

1.6 Constraints:

1.6.1	Location of work:

a.	The Contractor must perform the work at either the Contractor’s place of business or a location
determined by the Contractor.
b.	Travel
  i.	The Contractor will be required to travel to attend trainings as requested by the Project
Authority.

1.6.2	Language of Work:

The contractor must perform all work in English.

1.6.3 Security Requirements:

This contract includes the following security requirements:

IT Security Requirements Technical Document, to be included in the contract; and

SECURITY REQUIREMENT FOR CANADIAN SUPPLIER:  
PWGSC FILE No. 21280-26-5322937 – Revision 1

1. 	The Contractor must, at all times during the performance of the Contract, hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS), and obtain approved Document Safeguarding Capability at the level of PROTECTED B,  issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP), Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC). 

2. 	The Contractor personnel requiring access to PROTECTED information, assets, or sensitive site(s) must EACH hold a valid RELIABILITY STATUS, granted or approved by the CSP, PWGSC.

3.	The Contractor MUST NOT utilize its facilities to process, produce, or store PROTECTED information or assets until the CSP, PWGSC has issued written approval.

4.	The Contractor MUST NOT utilize its Information Technology systems to electronically process, produce, or store PROTECTED information until the CSP, PWGSC has issued written approval.  After approval has been granted or approved, these tasks may be performed at the level of PROTECTED B, including an IT Link at the level of PROTECTED B.

5. 	Subcontracts which contain security requirements are NOT to be awarded without the prior written permission of the CSP, PWGSC.

6. 	The Contractor must comply with the provisions of the:

	(a) 	Security Requirements Check List and Supplemental Security and Classification Guide (if applicable);
	(b) 	Contract Security Manual  (Latest Edition)

2. Criteria for assessment of the statement of capabilities (minimum essential requirements):

Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements:

Experience: 

a.	The organization must have at least 1 year of experience within the last 5 years, in project(s) involving counselling or intervention services with at-risk clients in an organization that delivers services to persons who have been referred to them by a professional or federal or provincial department.

b.	The proposed facilitator(s) must have at least 1 year of experience within the last 5 years in assessing human behaviour. 

c.	The proposed facilitator(s) must have at least 1 year of experience within the last 5 years in intervention or providing individual support, aimed at changing human behaviour, with multi faceted and socially disadvantaged clientele e.g. individuals who have experienced mental illness, been involved in the criminal justice system, substance abusers or have been homeless.

d.	The proposed facilitator(s) have at least 1 year experience in the last 5 years in facilitating group work (4 or more participants) to multi faceted or socially disadvantaged, clientele group(s), aimed at changing human behaviour e.g. those who have experienced mental illness, been involved in the criminal justice system, substance abusers or have been homeless.

e.	The proposed facilitator(s) must have at least 1 year experience in writing formal documents or assessments based on their work with the client(s). 

Academic qualifications:

The proposed facilitator(s) must be a graduate from a recognized college or university in a field that focuses on understanding and assessing human behaviour (such as a BA in the area of Psychology, Sociology, Social Work, Criminology or Education); 
- OR -
The proposed facilitator(s) must have a secondary school diploma or equivalent certificate.
	
The degree must have been obtained from a recognized Canadian university, college or high school, or the equivalent as established by a recognized Canadian academic credentials assessment service, if obtained outside Canada.

The list of recognized organizations can be found under the Canadian Information Centre for International Credentials web site.

3. Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement

This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement.

4. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business

This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers.

5. Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement(s)

This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement.

6. Justification for the Pre-Identified Supplier

There are no alternative service providers within Nova Scotia capable of delivering this specialized program to meet the specific needs of the federal offender population.

The supplier has successfully demonstrated their ability and expertise in helping with the offender’s safe rehabilitation and reintegration into the community. The supplier meets all the requirements of the program.

The pre-identified supplier meets all of the minimum essential requirements described in this ACAN.

7. Government Contracts Regulations Exception(s)

The following exception to the Government Contracts Regulations is invoked for this procurement under subsection: 

(d) only one person is capable of performing the contract.

8. Exclusions and/or Limited Tendering Reasons

This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement.

9. Ownership of Intellectual Property

There are no intellectual property terms in the contract.

10. Period of the proposed contract or delivery date

The proposed contract is for a period of ten (10) months, from December 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027 with an option to extend the contract for four (4) additional 1-year periods.

11. Cost estimate of the proposed contract

The estimated value of the contract, including option(s), is $303,500.00 (GST/HST extra).

12. Name and address of the pre-identified supplier

Name: The John Howard Society of Nova Scotia
Address: 1-541 Sackville Dr, Lower Sackville, NS  B4C 2S1

13. Suppliers' right to submit a statement of capabilities

Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to provide the goods, services or construction services described in the ACAN, may submit a statement of capabilities in writing to the contact person identified in this notice on or before the closing date and time of this notice. The statement of capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements.

14. Closing date and time for a submission of a statement of capabilities

The closing date and time for accepting statements of capabilities is November 25, 2026 at 2:00 PM ET.

15. Inquiries and submission of statements of capabilities

Inquiries and statement of capabilities are to be directed to:

Jolaine Amos, Procurement Officer
1045 Main St, Moncton, NB  E1C 1H1
Telephone: 506-787-4420
E-mail: Jolaine.Amos@csc-scc.gc.ca

This is a two-phase invitation process. Bidders responding to this Invitation to Tender (ITT) must submit a bid in two phases.

During Phase One, Bidders are invited to submit bids according to the selection procedure described in Phase One. Bidders will only have to submit the Phase One documents included in the ITT. Under Phase One, CSC will assess Bidders’ qualifications and experience in order to determine which bids are responsive. Once Phase One bid evaluation is completed, CSC will advise bidders of whether or not their bid is responsive.

During Phase Two, CSC will invite Bidders who submitted responsive bids for Phase One to submit a bid for Phase Two. Responsive Bidders will have to submit the Phase Two documents included in the ITT as part of Phase Two.

The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement for the Supply and Installation of
Mechanical Systems for a three-piece modular Ablutions Building with a total floor area of
approximately 1,920 sq. ft.
 
The majority of the work will be performed at the CORCAN Construction Compound located at the Matsqui Complex in Abbotsford, British Columbia, where the modular building will be fabricated, assembled and the Mechanical Systems substantially installed.
 
Upon completion of the fabrication and assembly phase, the three modules will be transported to the Nanaimo Military Camp in Nanaimo, British Columbia, where the Contractor will complete the remaining work, including final installation, connections, testing, commissioning, and any associated completion activities.

notices.title: Develop Wayfinding Strategy for Mississippi Lake National Wildlife Area (MLNWA), St Clair National Wildlife Area (SCNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA)

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Background
Canadian Wildlife Service (CWS) Ontario manages 10 National Wildlife Areas in Ontario.  Two of these, Prince Edward Point National Wildlife Area (PEPNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA) have also been designated as Connecting Canadians to Nature sites.  Out of more than 60 National Wildlife Areas across the country only 10 have been designated as Connecting Canadians to Nature sites. These 10 sites as well as select few of the other NWAs are open to the public and provide opportunities for people to experience and connect with nature. 
CWS Ontario is working to improve accessibility and enhance visitors’ experiences at publicly accessible NWAs in Ontario.  In 2025, a wayfinding strategy and upgrades to signage were completed at PEPNWA to improve accessibility for visitors.  CWS Ontario is now looking to implement similar improvements at other publicly accessible NWAs in the province using guidance developed for PEPNWA.

Objective
Develop Wayfinding Strategy for Mississippi Lake National Wildlife Area (MLNWA), St Clair National Wildlife Area (SCNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA) and complete signage designs as required based on outcomes of individual site visits and using guidance outlined in Design Brief (Appendix B) and Wayfinding Signage Design Intent (Appendix C) previously prepared for PEPNWA.

The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide Primary Care Physician services for the Beaver Creek Institution – Medium Security and Beaver Creek Institution – Minimum Security in the Ontario Region.

Objectives: The Contractor (Primary Care Physician) must provide integrated patient centred medical services to  patients in collaboration with the Institution's inter-disciplinary health care team that includes, but is not limited to: nurses (nurse practitioners, registered nurses, registered psychiatric nurses, licensed practical nurses, registered practical nurses), primary care physicians, social workers, dentists, denturists, infectious disease physician specialist, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, psychologists, psychiatrists, behavioural science technicians, mental health providers, psychoeducators, personal support workers, client care attendants, optometrist, physiotherapists, x-ray technologists, foot care specialists, occupational therapists, administrative personnel and other healthcare professionals.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Standing Offer for Energy Performance Contract Procurement and Financial Advisory Services
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform consultants of an upcoming Standing Offer opportunity.

The purpose of this APN is to allow consultants to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential Standing Offer, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested consultants to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances.

Please note that there is no guarantee that this Standing Offer will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional upon funding approval by DND.

APN Number: EPFS2601
Approximate Estimate: 800,000$
Anticipated Posting: January 2027

Description: Energy Performance Contract Procurement and Financial Advisory Services

The Consultant will be required to provide “as and when required” procurement and financial advisory services in support of Energy Performance Contracts (EPCs).
The services may include, but are not limited to, the following:

	Review and provide procurement and financial advice on the contractual documents including the Request for Proposal (RFP) financial evaluation criteria;
	Support DCC in preparing draft responses to financial questions from Proponents during the procurement phase;
	Review and provide advice on the financial evaluation framework to assess the Proponent’s financial capabilities;
	Assist DCC with the evaluation of the financial component of the Proponents proposals;
	Support DCC in the review and analysis of the financial proposal received following the feasibility study;
	Assist in the negotiation and finalizing the final terms of the contract.

The objective is to select one (1) consultant capable of providing deliverables in both official languages (English and French).
The estimated value of the Standing Offer is approximately $500,000 over an initial two (2)-year period, with the option to extend the Standing Offer for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods and to increase its value by an additional $300,000 at any time. The total estimated potential value of the Standing Offer is approximately $800,000 over four (4) years.

3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for the issuance of a Standing Offer, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, consultants that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.

5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant:

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and
	has submitted a proposal,  

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Consultants that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:

Patricia Biernat
Procurement Specialist
Defence Construction Canada
819-500-8074
Patricia.Biernat@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Construction Management Services, Whitehorse cadet training centre 
whitehorse, yukon 
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Whitehorse, Yukon.

The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES

The objective of this contract is to recapitalize both vertical and horizontal infrastructure at the Whitehorse Cadet Training Centre (WCTC) through a multi-year program.

The existing WCTC site includes a diverse portfolio of facilities comprising 39 buildings with a total floor area of approximately 5,000 m². These facilities include barracks with associated ablution areas, classrooms, a combined kitchen/dining/administration building, a large storage warehouse, and various workshops and auxiliary support structures.

The recapitalization program will encompass the renovation of existing buildings, as well as the demolition and reconstruction of selected facilities, to modernize and enhance the overall functionality of the site.

Project delivery will be undertaken using a Construction Management (CM) contract.

The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project.

To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the CM contract. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities.

It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN: APN_NPYKCM01
Approximate Estimate: $50M
Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027

3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for contract award, a proponent  will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS)

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors  that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.


5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and
	has submitted a proposal.  

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Contractors  that do not submit a proposal  will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:



Eric Ndayambaza
Coordinator, Contract Services
Defence Construction Canada
Eric.Ndayambaza@dcc-cdc.gc.ca
Email: +(1) 343-576-9347




7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.

This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en.

Challenge title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance
Challenge sponsor: Shared Services Canada (SSC) 

Funding Mechanism: Contract
MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE:
Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge.

Phase 2: 
• The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required.
• The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report).
• Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1

This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes.
Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge.

Travel: No travel required. 
Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference.
Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference.
Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference.

Problem Statement:

Challenge Statement Summary
The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice.
The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices.
Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. 
The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight.

Details:

Essential (mandatory) Outcomes
The proposed solution must:

1.	Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and  be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required.

2.	Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization.
2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks).
2B. Demonstrate how governance information can be collected, aggregated and maintained across multiple systems through APIs, connectors and data exchange mechanisms.
2C. Leverage open standards and documented interfaces to reduce dependency on proprietary technologies enabling interoperability across diverse enterprise environments.

3.	Demonstrate how administrative, support and access to governance information and data can be restricted, monitored and controlled in accordance with the GoC requirements.
3A. Enable organizations to define and manage data residency requirements, retention, access and deletion of policies and information without vendor intervention.

4.	Enable assessment and reassessment of registered AI systems applicable AI governance requirements, policies, standards, directives while supporting reassessment when governance requirements, assessment frameworks are added modified, replaced or retired. The solution must demonstrate the ability to translate AI governance requirements into traceable controls assess whether applicable controls have been satisfied and identify non-conformities.
4A. Enable authorized users to add, modify, version, replace or retire governance requirements and assessment frameworks to individual AI systems or groups. Demonstrate compliance assessment at minimum against the Policy on Service and Digital,  Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessment, AI Strategy and AI ethics and responsibilities. 
4B. Demonstrate the ability to add, modify, version, replace and retire governance requirements, controls and assessment criteria, and assign them to individual AI systems or groups of AI systems. while supporting the application of different assessment criteria to different AI systems based on their intended use, risk profile or governance requirements Offerors are encouraged to prove extensibility to additional internationally recognized governance frameworks and standards, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the EU Act.
4C. Generate human-readable explanations of assessment and reassessment results. Each finding must identify the applicable requirement, evidence considered, assessment result and confidence score or a certainty measure. user.
4D. Collect, link, and retain assurance artefacts including control mapping, assessment records, evidence references, approvals, exceptions, attestations, remediation actions and audit histories. The system must identify whether each artifact was provided by an authorised individual [Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)].
4E. Provide measurable results and clearly distinguish between results when performing a compliance assessments to determine whether compliance is met, partially met, not met, not applicable and unable to determine.

5.	Allow for authorised reviewers to validate reject, modify or annotate findings and retain and audit log history for decisions.

6.	Support the assessment and reassessment of risks associated with data, models and AI-generated outputs and incorporate the resulting information into governance assessments and assurance activities.
6A. Support assessment of data related risks and quality measures relevant to the registered AI system including the establishment of baseline measures and thresholds to maintain a traceable record of issues. 
6B. Enable organizations to define, evaluate and reassess risk, performance and quality measures appropriate to a registered AI system. including configurable measures, thresholds, and evaluation criteria to maintain a traceable record of assessment outcomes.
6C. Support the evaluation and monitoring of AI-generated outputs against criteria appropriate to the system’s intended use and identified risks including accuracy, quality, fairness, consistency, safety, and alignment with defined operational requirements. 


Additional Outcomes
The proposed solution should:

1.  Support deployment in on-premises, private cloud, and Canadian-hosted cloud environments without requiring significant architectural modification.

2. 	Provide bilingual functionality, including user interfaces, documentation, reporting, and governance workflows, in both English an French.                                                                                                                                                   

3. 	Support multiple organizations, departments, or domains within a shared platform while enabling independent governance policies, controls, reporting, and oversight for each tenant.

4. Generate governance reports, alerts, and notifications and integrate with enterprise collaboration, communication, and ticketing/case management systems.

Background and context
As Shared Services Canada (SSC) expands the use of AI solutions, including generative and Agentic AI, there is a growing need for a consistent, centralized, and scalable approach to AI governance. Current governance activities may rely on separate processes, manual tracking, and fragmented documentation, which can limit real-time visibility into AI system inventories, risk posture, compliance status, policy alignment, and decision-making evidence.

notices.buyer: Department of Public Works and Government Services (PSPC)

sections.text:

*Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30, 2026*

This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en

Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal.

Steps to apply:
Step 1: Read this challenge.
Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872
Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/weak-magnetic-anomaly-detection-defence-and-security?auHash=1sFpxB6DzXI5S5IfIex1eysacfiS2cUIMVE1Eeit0EQ

ISED is seeking a novel magnetometer (either quantum or classical or a combination thereof) that provides advantage over existing capabilities either in sensitivity, specificity, or Size, Weight, Power and Cost (SWaP-C), and multi-domain employability.

Challenge sponsor:
Innovation, Sciences et Développement économique Canada (ISDE) 

Funding mechanism:
Contract

Opening date:
October 30, 2026

Closing date:
November 27, 2026 14:00 Eastern time

Challenge
Problem statement
Canada has a requirement for magnetic anomaly detection for defence and security. Traditional magnetometers, such as fluxgate sensors, have been used for decades to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. A fluxgate magnetometer is a relatively simple classical device: it consists of a coil of wire wrapped around a core material and detects changes in magnetic flux passing through the sensor. While reliable, these classical sensors face inherent limitations in size, sensitivity, accuracy, and long term stability. Quantum magnetometers, by contrast, leverage the principles of quantum mechanics and promise the ability to achieve superior performance. They offer enhanced sensitivity, improved accuracy and stability, and in some cases even reduced size and weight compared to their classical counterparts.
There is a lack of suitably mature quantum sensors in the commercial space. The government of Canada has identified a need to develop a device or system consisting of hardware and software and a quantum sensor or a mix of classical and quantum sensors capable of sensing nanotesla (nT) or even femtotesla (fT) magnetic signals that can be used for a myriad of commercial, medical, and defence applications. In scanning the research underway, there appears to be interest in various means for the sensing of magnetic fields, including but not limited to Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUID), Superconducting Quantum Interference Filter (SQIF), and (Nitrogen Vacancy (NV) diamond. In addition to this we are led to believe that Rydberg atoms, typically framed for electric field detection can be reconfigured and/or adapted for magnetic field detection as well. We are also aware of another technology termed Spin-Exchange Relaxation-Free (SERF) which is very sensitive, but so sensitive as to be problematic to employ. This investigation seeks to explore nT and even fT sensitivities.

Desired outcomes and considerations
Essential (mandatory) outcomes
The proposed solution must: 
1.	Essential range and direction finding considerations 
Demonstrate sensing capabilities of magnetic anomalies in close proximity where distance (d) is greater than or equal to (=) 2 meters (m) with a relative error less than 10%. The device must provide azimuth to +/- 5 degrees, and an inclination of +/- 5 degrees.
2.	Sensitivity 
Produce a prototype capable of a minimum of 500 picotesla (pT) sensitivity with a target of 10 fT. 
3.	Specificity
The device must be able to separate a target signal from background noise.  A sensitive magnetometer will detect a plethora of magnetic fields in a given cluttered environment, but the user will be interested in the absence or presence of a target signal. The device must detect and identify three specific Steel 1018 ferromagnetic targets at a minimum distance of 10 meter through free space. It must achieve a 95% true positive rate (TPR) for both detecting the presence of a target and classifying which specific target is present.
4.	Rough characterization 
Demonstrate ability to characterize the nature of the source in rough order of magnitude – i.e. point source vs larger objects +/- 5 centimeters (cm).
5.	Latency 
Readout less than or equal to (=) 200 milliseconds (ms) meaning sensing, ranging, azimuth, and inclination reading allowing dynamic device sensor use for object or enclosure survey. This 200 ms is the total time from sensing to displaying the result to the human user.  This time includes physical sensing, processing to the point the user is provided useful data. 
6.	Sense through barrier capability
Ability for device to sense through paramagnetic barrier materials such as walls (including but not limited to wood, gypsum board, plaster, insulation material) with some barriers inundated with clutter from other materials such as steel studs, nails, screws, pipes and other ferromagnetic materials.
7.	Prototype description
All parts/components fully integrated in one system of systems, including but not limited to power, API/software, hardware (sensor, cooler – if applicable).
8.	Power
Power consumption must be 50 W or less. Integrated replaceable power supply offering at least eight (8) hours of cordless and continued operation at temperatures ranging between 16°C and 40°C at a relative humidity between 30 and 60%.
9.	Human factors
Must be lightweight and compact/portable (e.g.; hand-carried, “shoulderable”, body worn).  
10.	Size and weight
Volumetric dimensions =117,232 cm^3 (77 x 52.5 x 29 cm); maximum weight = 15Kg.
11.	Environmental considerations
The initial device must be designed at least for indoor use at temperatures ranging between 16°C to 30°C with relative humidity between 30-60% 
12.	Per unit cost
Must show that a finished device can be made under $60,000 CAD. 

Additional Outcomes 
The proposed solution should:  
1.	Desirable range 
It is desirable to have a device that has greater standoff range in excess of 2m. The accuracy in ranging the MA would ideally be less than 1% relative error. Maximum sensing distance is desirable. The device should provide an azimuth to +/- 1 degree, and an inclination of +/- 1 degree.
2.	Rough characterization
The device provides a rough but human interpretable shape of the object, that allows the object to be characterized or even identified. 
3.	Sensitivity 
Produce a prototype capable of surpassing 10 fT sensitivity.
4.	Specificity 
Ability to characterize and identify magnetic anomalies (objects with a known magnetic signature). 
5.	Quiet 
Device should be silent (vibration/audible signature).
6.	Desired Configuration 
Device does not emit acoustic, electromagnetic (EM), and/or heat signature. Can run in both low and high humidity in temperature extremes from -20 to +40C, under conditions of vibration, and through cluttered barriers (e.g.; barrier material convoluted with wiring, and magnetic structural material)
7.	Target Scale 
Desirable to be used against both large (room sized) and small (hardware or package sized) enclosures or objects.
8.	Static vs oscillating field detection 
Ability to differentiate between static and oscillating magnetic fields.
9.	Characterization of magnetic anomalies/sources 
Ability to characterize and identify magnetic anomalies. Ability to discern shape and size +/- 1 cm.
10.	Human factor / accessibility considerations 
Device should be suitably adapted as to be easy to train on, easy to use (intuitive), and be in a shape or form factor that is amenable for the operator to use in both open and confined settings. The device should be man portable. Human factor considerations will be rated by a panel of experts and multi-criteria analysis. ( Multi-criteria analysis is a type of option rating technique where by each option is scored against different criteria.  For example, one of the best known techniques is Simple Multi-attribute Rating Technique.  Whereas essential outcomes are high level mandatory requirements that must be achieved, a scoring system could be devised to rate different prototypes based on criteria found in the additional outcomes.)  
11.	Environmental considerations  
Produce a more robust device for outdoor land use capable of -40-40 °C, over a wide range of Canadian climate conditions is desired. This includes extremes in humidity, hot, cold, and use in wet or dusty conditions.

Background and context
Magnetometry and magnetic sensors play an important role in the detection and measurement of magnetic fields around us. Applications for use exist in many industries and interest areas are not limited to natural resource discovery (including critical minerals), monitoring of the environment, healthcare, defence, and security.

For natural resource discovery magnetic sensors are used to help sense and identify mineral deposits including copper, nickel, iron, and gold. Indeed, the same technology has promise in the search for rare earth minerals which are essential to commercial, academic, and security uses.

Magnetic sensors also play an important role in environmental monitoring. They can be used to track ocean currents, detect geologic activity, and observe other natural processes. By measuring subtle variations in magnetic fields and related proxy signals, magnetometers provide valuable insights into changes in the Earth’s climate.

In healthcare, many imaging technologies—most notably magnetic resonance imaging—depend on generating and detecting subtle perturbations in magnetic flux. Researchers are now exploring the use of nitrogen vacancy diamonds integrated into existing MRI systems, with the goal of achieving higher sensitivity and improved image resolution. 

Maximum contract value and travel
Phase 2
·	Maximum funding: $2,000,000.00 CAD
·	Project duration: Up to 24 months
·	Estimated number of contracts: 1

This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contracts for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 2 awards will be made by Canada based on factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities, and availability of funds. The Government of Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes.

Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge.

All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference.

Progress review meeting(s)
Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference.

Final review meeting
All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference.

Limited to firms on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). This solicitation of offer is limited to offerors registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR).

Background
Pursuant to section 46 of the Nunavut Act, the Auditor General is required to annually audit accounts and financial statements of the Government of Nunavut. As part of this requirement, the Office of the Auditor General of Canada (the OAG) produces a variety of documents, including the annual Nunavut report, that need to be translated from English into Inuktitut, in either the North or South Baffin dialect. Translated documents will also need to be edited and updated.

Objective
The objective of this procurement process is for the Contractor to provide timely, consistent and reliable English to Inuktitut translation and editing services for Nunavut reports, opening statements and communication products that will be presented by the OAG to the government of Nunavut. The OAG will also require translation or editing of other types of documents varying in length and topic throughout the year, including consolidated financial statements.

The Contractor will perform all work from its own facilities. No travel is anticipated for the duration of the resulting contract.  In executing the work, Contractor managed devices, tools and IT services will only be used when processing unprotected information. The OAG will provide a laptop computer and access to the OAG network when the work requires access to protected information.

Term
The period of the Contract is from 1-April-2027 to 31-March-2029 inclusive, with the option to extend the Contract for up to two (2) additional two-year periods.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) for User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing 

This bid solicitation 1000505276/B cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000505276/A dated November 03, 2025 with a closing of December 03, 2025 at 02:00 PM EDT. 
The solicitation is being reissued as the previous solicitations resulted in non compliant bids. Unless otherwise stated herein, all terms and conditions of the original solicitation remain unchanged.

The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) intends to enter into a contract with a single contractor for access to a user testing software platform to test CRA content on Canada.ca with the Canadian public, as well as certain niche audiences such as business owners, families with children, and other demographics as required. The ability to test with persons who use assistive reading and navigation technologies is not within scope for this requirement and has been solicited under a separate procurement by the CRA. The objective is to assess the ease with which users can find information and successfully complete tasks on Canada.ca and to identify any difficulties that users face in navigating CRA content so that solutions can be proposed and implemented to improve those performance measures.
This requirement also includes irrevocable options to procure additional quantities of test requests to be used within the User Testing Software Platform annual entity license for the User Testing Software Platform for User Experience Testing.  
The period of any resulting contract will be for two (2) years with CRA retaining the irrevocable option to extend the period of the contract for up to five (5) additional one (1) year periods.
A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid with the lowest bid evaluation price will be recommended for contract award.
Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French.
Conditional Set-Aside Under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business
•	This procurement may be conditionally set aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business.
•	In order to be considered for the set-aside, the Bidder must certify that it qualifies as an Indigenous business as defined under PSIB and that it will comply with all requirements of PSIB. If bids from two (2) or more Indigenous businesses are compliant with the terms of the Request for Proposal, the contracting authority will limit the competition to those Indigenous businesses and will not consider bids from any non-Indigenous businesses that may have been submitted.
•	For more information on Indigenous business requirements of the Set-aside Program for Indigenous Business, refer to Eligibility for Indigenous procurement set aside and Procurement information for Indigenous business owners
Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: 
Christian.Nkezurukundo@cra-arc.gc.ca
Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to:
Canada Revenue Agency
Bid Receiving Unit
BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca
Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Appendix 3: Standard Instructions - Goods or Services - Competitive Requirements of the Request for Proposal. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA.
The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement.

General Safety Training Services
British Columbia

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform consultants of an upcoming contract opportunity at various locations in British Columbia.

The purpose of this APN is to allow consultants to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested [contractors and consultants] to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

APN Number:88336
Approximate Estimate: $1,000,000
Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027

Description:
It is the Department of National Defence/Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) policy to maintain a General Safety Program (GSP), which ensures that safety considerations are incorporated into every aspect of departmental operations, training, and support activities. The Consultant will be responsible to maintain (if necessary) and deliver training courses on an as needed basis to DND/CAF in the courses falling within a General Safety training category. notices.buyer: Department of Public Works and Government Services (PSPC)

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.***

This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en

Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal.

Steps to apply:
Step 1: Read this challenge.
Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872
Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/high-altitude-platform-system-ultra-long-range-wireless-backhaul

The Department of National Defence (DND), Shared Services Canada (SSC) and National Research Council of Canada (NRC) are seeking the development of a solution that will extend the reach of ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e. over-the-horizon ranges) using High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS).
Challenge sponsor: National Research Council (NRC)
Funding mechanism: Contract
Opening date : October 20, 2026
Closing date : December 1, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time

Problem statement
The Government of Canada recognizes the critical role that advanced communication technologies play in supporting national defence, public safety, and the security of Canadians. Reliable and resilient connectivity in dangerous, remote, and sparsely populated regions is essential for effective defence operations, emergency response, and border monitoring. However, delivering such connectivity remains a significant challenge due to Canada’s vast geography, low population densities, and extreme environmental conditions.

The Department of National Defence, Shared Services Canada and National Research Council of Canada are seeking the development of a solution that leverages High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) to provide ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e., over-the-horizon ranges). This capability will enhance communications under harsh weather or challenging terrain in theatres of conflict, in remote areas, and isolated regions with little to no current connectivity. The ultimate goal is to improve secure, high-speed communications for Canadian defence, surveillance, and emergency operations while also potentially benefiting civilian emergency response connectivity needs.

The successful applicant is responsible for securing a demonstration site as well as a Special Flight Operations Certificate (SFOC) clearance from Transport Canada to demonstrate the HAPS capabilities.

Desired outcomes and considerations
Essential (mandatory) outcomes
The proposed solution must:
1.	Demonstrate the capability to travel from the surface up to 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers and travel laterally within the corridor of 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers.
2.	Operate at a specified, nominal, fixed point relative to the Earth for an extended period (minimum of 3 days).
3.	Launch, deploy, and operate from land or water-based environments.
4.	Provide a minimum of 100 Watts to support the deployment of long-range sensors.
5.	Deliver high-bandwidth, high-availability, ultra-low latency wireless connectivity comparable to current offerings (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) in the telecommunications industry.
6.	Support current (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) wireless systems and infrastructure.
7.	Provide a minimum of 1000 km² service area coverage and a minimum of 200 km² of transit area coverage based on usage demands.
8.	Be deployable within 6 hours for heavier-than-air HAPS or within 24 hours for lighter-than-air HAPS.
9.	Incorporate automated decision-making for flight maneuvers and operations.
10.	Operate at cold temperatures between -50 to at least -70 degrees Celsius.
Additional outcomes
The proposed solution should:
1.	Have a power management system that optimizes power consumption and adapts to usage demand.
2.	Be capable of continuous power generation and recharging during ground operations and flight through renewable energy sources.
3.	Have non-assisted launch and land capability from land or water-based environments.
4.	Support next generation wireless systems and infrastructure.
5.	Maintain wireless connectivity in the presence of intentional and unintentional wireless channel interference.
6.	Provide communications link security features and platform hardening to prevent signal interception, hacking and unauthorized platform hijacking.
7.	Demonstrate the ability to daisy chain the signal using intra-HAPS (i.e HAPS group 1 to HAPS group2), and/or inter-HAPS (between individual HAPS).
8.	Support backhauling requirements for future wireless networks.
9.	Complement the terrestrial communication infrastructures.
10.	Minimize the amount of traditional backhaul hopping.
11.	Support point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, and mesh links.

Background and context
High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) are unmanned vehicles designed to operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 20 to 50 kilometers above the Earth's surface. HAPS are classified into two main types: Lighter-than-air (LTA) platforms and Heavier-than-air (HTA) platforms. LTA platforms include balloons and airships characterized by low energy consumption but has limited maneuverability. On the other hand, HTA platforms which include light unmanned aircrafts that rely on electric motors to generate and maintain lift offer greater maneuverability but have payload weight restrictions and can have an energy deficit issue as a result of prolonged dark periods during winter months at higher latitudes.

HAPS offer several advantages such as its ability to be airborne for long durations and less expensive to operate compared to satellites. Since HAPS fly at lower altitudes than satellites, they are able to provide low latency data communications. The propulsion systems for HAPS generally use sustainable energy sources which have a lower environmental impact than rocket launches for satellites.

Presently, existing wireless backhaul technologies have limitations in terms of coverage and during emergency situations for remote areas, nomadic users, and scattered populations. A merging solution between HAPS and ULR (Ultra-Long-Range) wireless backhaul, offering broadband services, would be a great benefit to a wide range of populations, especially in times of crisis and during emergency situations where traditional telecommunication services suffer outages. Additionally, HAPS are highly effective platforms for enhancing military communications and remote sensing capabilities. They can be used to complement military satcom infrastructure, offering capabilities in intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. When equipped with high-resolution cameras, radars, and signals intelligence systems (SIGINT), HAPS provide continuous coverage of areas of interest.
